sections.label: The Models
paragraphs: Kimi K3 on max effort against GPT-6 Astra on low effort. Game 9 of ten, drafted fresh.
The most lopsided game of the series. Astra finished on 32 life having gained twelve and grown a single creature to 13/13; Kimi never dealt a point of damage to it after turn 3.

sections.label: Draft
paragraphs: Picks and reasoning are [[view:draft|here]], the final lists [[view:decks|here]].

Astra drafted the Ally deck this time: [[card:Earth King's Lieutenant]] and [[card:South Pole Voyager]] with [[card:Invasion Reinforcements]] and [[card:Katara, the Fearless]], who doubles Ally triggers. Every Ally that enters pumps the Lieutenant, gains life and draws.

Kimi drafted Dimir with [[card:North Pole Patrol]] and [[card:Tiger-Seal]] as defensive pieces and [[card:Deadly Precision]] as its removal — a deck built to trade one-for-one against a deck that does not trade.

rounds.label: Turn 1
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] takes the play, keeps four lands with two strong two-drops, and leads on a tapped [[card:Kyoshi Village]].
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] reads the tapped green-white land correctly and notes in its own log that Astra is on Allies.

rounds.label: Turn 2
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] spends four attempts trying to cast [[card:Earth King's Lieutenant]], each one cancelled on which colour the Village should produce, and eventually gives up and casts [[card:South Pole Voyager]] instead so the turn is not wasted.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts [[card:Forecasting Fortune Teller]] as a 1/3 blocker.

rounds.label: Turn 3
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] gets the Lieutenant down on its second try, which immediately pumps the Voyager to 3/3, and attacks. The Fortune Teller blocks and dies.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] is already out of blockers.

rounds.label: Turn 4
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] casts [[card:Invasion Reinforcements]], which grows the Lieutenant again, gains life and draws a card, and adds [[card:Airbender Ascension]] — airbending its own creature for value rather than using it as removal.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] has no creatures and passes. Astra is on 21 and climbing.

rounds.label: Turns 5 and 6
paragraphs: The Ally engine compounds. [[card:Katara, the Fearless]] arrives to double every Ally trigger, [[card:Airbender Ascension]] starts blinking [[card:Rowdy Snowballers]] at end step to stun Kimi's blockers, and [[card:Earth King's Lieutenant]] grows with each one.

[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] holds at 14 behind [[card:North Pole Patrol]] and [[card:Tiger-Seal]], with no way to attack into a board that gains life faster than it can deal damage. Astra passes 28 life.

rounds.label: Turn 7
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] goes for lethal and clears the way first: [[card:Honest Work]] on [[card:North Pole Patrol]] to strip the tap ability that is holding the game together.

[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] plays the best card of its game in response — it pays the Patrol's waterbend cost to tap the now-13/13 trampling Lieutenant before the aura resolves. The alpha strike still deals 13, but Kimi survives on 1 life instead of dying.
[[player:PilotB|Astra]] blinks [[card:Rowdy Snowballers]] at end step anyway, with Katara doubling the trigger, stunning two of Kimi's remaining blockers for the following turn.

rounds.label: Turn 8
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Astra]] attacks with everything into a board of three blockers. The 13/13 is blocked by a 3/3, tramples ten over, and the rest is academic. Kimi dies on turn 15; Astra finishes on 32.

There was never a turn where Kimi could have traded profitably. Its deck answers cards one at a time and Astra's deck produces two or three triggers per card — the same Ally engine Kimi itself had won game 1 with, on the other side of the table. The one genuinely excellent play of the game, tapping a 13/13 in response to the aura meant to disable the tapper, bought exactly one turn.
